title: Fly to Lake Saiful Muluk
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: In the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa lies one of Pakistan's most famous lakes: Saiful Muluk.
We start above the town of Naran, at the northern end of the valley.
From here, a mountain road climbs east, towards the lake.
And there it is: Lake Saiful Muluk, at about three thousand two hundred and twenty-four metres above sea level.
It is often called Pakistan's highest alpine lake, with cold, clear, greenish-blue water.
Glaciers and snowy peaks surround it, including Malika Parbat, the Queen of the Mountains.
The lake takes its name from a legend. Prince Saif-ul-Malook of Egypt fell in love with a fairy princess, Badi-ul-Jamal.
In the story, a white giant held her captive, and when the lovers escaped, his fury caused a great flood.
Locals say nearby Ansoo Lake was formed from the giant's tears, and that the couple still dance above the water on full-moon nights.
The poet Mian Muhammad Bakhsh told this tale in a famous Punjabi poem.
The best time to visit is June to September. In winter, heavy snow freezes the lake.
